class.name: NetwPredictionHandle
class.brief_description: Prediction settings and diagnostics for one [NetwEntity].
class.description: Access this handle through [member NetwEntity.prediction]. It stores entity-level prediction settings and the latest comparison against authoritative state. [codeblock] var pred := NetwEntity.of(self).prediction pred.archetype = NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY pred.witness_contacts = _sample_contacts pred.breach_response = NetwPredict.BREACH_RESPONSE_DEMOTE [/codeblock] Declare field-level behavior, including tolerances and recovery rules, with [NetwPropertyConfig]. The step, the schedule and the entities this one runs with are on [member NetwEntity.simulation], and [member NetwSimulationHandle.mode] says how this peer runs the entity. Prediction registers only on an entity with a [method NetwPropertyConfig.state] row, because the state is what it compares and restores. An entity that declares an [member archetype] with no state row reports one error when its owner is ready and is not predicted. A [MultiplayerSynchronizer] may provide scene defaults. Later assignments in code override those values. [member stats] counts corrections. The signals report each divergence, episode and recovery as it happens. [method reachability] says what each declaration actually reaches.

method.name: bind_entity
method.description: Binds the entity this handle belongs to. Called by the entity record's factory, which is the only thing that creates a handle.

method.name: entity
method.description: The entity this handle declares prediction for, or [code]null[/code] once that entity is gone.

method.name: is_registered
method.description: True once an engine is attached to this handle, which is how a caller tells an entity that is actually predicting from one that has only been configured.

method.name: notify_contact
method.description: Opens a window of [member collision_cooldown_ticks] during which a recovery smaller than [member teleport_threshold] is held off, so the brief disagreement a collision causes is not corrected through. Call it from the controlling client when the predicted body registers a collision. It does nothing with no engine attached.

method.name: reachability
method.description:
What this entity's declarations actually reach, field by field, or an empty [Dictionary] before the entity is attached to an engine. A declaration can be legal, be accepted, and still do nothing. [method NetwPropertyConfig.carry_step] under [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_TICK] is rejected the first time it is used and never tried again, a [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only] field that is free to trigger asks for corrections no smaller restore may write, and an [method NetwPropertyConfig.epsilon] on a field no comparison reads bounds nothing. This is where a game finds that out while wiring rather than in a capture. [codeblock] var report := entity.prediction.reachability() for key: StringName in report[&"fields"]: var row: Dictionary = report[&"fields"][key] var model: Dictionary = row[&"forward_model"] if not model[&"live"] and model[&"kind"] != &"none": print(key, " forward model is not live, ", model[&"why"])
print(report[&"breach"]) print(report[&"findings"]) [/codeblock] [code]fields[/code] is keyed by property, and each row carries the following. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴class which NetwPropertySet.PropertyClass it is ┠╴triggers whether it can force a correction on its own ┠╴tolerance the epsilon in force, and who declared it ┠╴teleport_at the teleport distance, and who declared it ┠╴in_tier whether it is in the tier being compared ┠╴operators what may write it during a recovery ┖╴forward_model {kind, live, why} [/codeblock] [code]findings[/code] is the same list the wiring report prints, so a test asserts on it rather than on log text. Everything here is read from what this handle already carries, so a caller gathers no arguments.

method.name: resolved_recovery_policy
method.description: The [enum NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy] this entity recovers under. It never returns [constant NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_AUTO], which it resolves against the body. A physics body at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME] that declares [constant NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY] resolves [constant NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER].

method.name: sensor
simulate_frame
method.description: Runs one drive for an entity scheduled per frame. It does nothing for an entity scheduled per tick, or with no engine attached. The transition it writes is labelled from the clock exactly as the session's own frame drive labels one, so driving an entity by hand and letting the session drive it produce the same transition.

method.name: simulate_tick
method.description: Steps prediction or consumption for [param tick], and does nothing with no engine attached.

members.member: How many ticks behind the newest input the acknowledgement is, updated every tick. On the owning client it is the span a restore has to project across, and [member NetwSimulationHandle.max_restore_ticks] caps it. On the server it is the backlog waiting to be consumed, and [member max_consume_per_tick] drains it. A healthy link holds it near zero, and a growing value means the server is falling behind.

The set of prediction settings this entity starts from, or [constant NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_NONE]. A preset is a starting point. Writing it applies that set's recovery settings and [member NetwSimulationHandle.schedule] outright, and anything written afterwards refines them. [constant NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_SCRIPTED] writes [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_TICK]. [constant NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY] writes [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME] and [constant NetwSimulationHandle.RESTORE_EXTRAPOLATED]. A scene declaring prediction on its [MultiplayerSynchronizer] therefore applies its archetype first and writes only the values it actually moved, so a value left at its default cannot overwrite the preset it was meant to refine. No preset sets [member breach_response], because it is the one recovery setting that stops speculation at a witnessed contact and follows authority until the entity is reseeded. A game that wants that says so itself.

What this entity does the moment it touches something it was not predicted to touch. It is armed only when [member witness_contacts] declares how contacts are observed. [constant NetwPredict.BREACH_RESPONSE_DEMOTE] follows authority from then on while the entity keeps sending its input.

How many ticks [method notify_contact] holds off corrections for. A collision makes the predicted and the authoritative body genuinely differ for a few ticks while both settle, and correcting through that fights the physics. A disagreement past [member teleport_threshold] still snaps.

How many ticks of input the server keeps in hand rather than consuming the queue to empty. Input arrives on two clocks that run independently, so it drifts across the server's consume boundary, and a server holding nothing spare alternates ticks where the entity does not step at all with ticks where it drains a burst. This is a target the server keeps to rather than a warm-up it does once. A tick whose queue has fallen to the target consumes nothing and rebuilds the slack instead, and [member max_consume_per_tick] trims a burst back to the target rather than to zero. [codeblock lang=text] span > buffer consume, draining toward buffer + 1 0 < span <= buffer hold, and the slack rebuilds span <= 0 starved, no input exists [/codeblock] Every tick of depth costs a tick of input latency, and a hold delays one input by one step. A value of [code]0[/code] consumes inputs as they arrive, with no slack to absorb any drift.

How far this entity may drift before an arriving state triggers a correction. A field needing a tolerance of its own declares one with [method NetwPropertyConfig.epsilon], which replaces this for that field alone.

Which version of the unmoving world this entity simulates against, or [code]-1[/code] while none is declared. Raising it reopens the tolerance window, because two peers cannot have taken a change to the world on the same transition. Like [member sensors] this describes the world rather than the group the entity is simulated with, so it never enters the entity into a fingerprint comparison.

How far the server may fall behind the newest input before it stops catching up one tick at a time and jumps to the live edge. The server never steps over a missing tick, so across a gap it gains one tick per server tick while the client keeps producing one per tick. A gap therefore never closes on its own and the acknowledgement stays behind forever, which reads as an entity that simulates and is never corrected. The usual way to open one is a client whose clock re-anchors after it has already produced input, joining a session that has been running a while. [codeblock lang=text] within the ceiling walk forward, filling holes one at a time past the ceiling re-open at the newest input, less consume_buffer_ticks [/codeblock] Input skipped that way is a second old and no longer worth simulating. A value of [code]0[/code] turns the recovery off and lets the server fall as far behind as it falls.

How many queued input ticks one frame may fold together when a backlog has built up, for an entity at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME]. The client produces one input per tick, so the default of [code]1[/code] keeps the two in step. A higher value lets a frame skip past inputs that have already arrived rather than working through the backlog one frame at a time. Folding never steps over a lost tick, and folded inputs are skipped rather than simulated, so it is never extra work. An entity at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_TICK] ignores this and advances by exactly one per tick, because authority may not run a transition its own clock has not reached.
What the server does about an input tick that never arrived, as a [enum NetwPredict.MissingInput] value.
Whether this entity is corrected on its own or together with the entities its [member NetwEntity.simulation] selects, as a [enum NetwPredict.Reconcile] value.

The [enum NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy] this entity declares. The default [constant NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_AUTO] picks one from the body, and [method resolved_recovery_policy] returns the policy the entity actually recovers under.

How many transitions authority leaves standing in the queue instead of replaying, for an entity at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME]. It is latency added to every command and it buys nothing back, which is why it defaults to zero. Authority replays at most one transition per frame, so it can never drain faster than the owner fills, and a reserve that cannot be spent faster than it is refilled absorbs no jitter. Every tick of depth is another tick of [member ack_age_ticks] behind every recovery. [codeblock lang=text] depth > buffer replay one transition (consumed) 0 < depth <= buffer hold, spending nothing (held) depth == 0 the queue is dry (starved) [/codeblock] At the default of zero the middle row cannot happen, so a frame either replays the transition it has or reports that it has none. Raise it only to trade acknowledgement latency for a later replay position. It will not smooth arrival, because what covers a dry frame is depth an earlier burst already built, at any buffer including zero.

The world facts this entity's transition reads, by name. Each sampler is called once before each drive and recorded with it, which is what lets a divergence be blamed on the world rather than left unexplained. [method sensor] reads the sample back. A sampler that cannot be called is skipped when it would have been sampled rather than rejected here, so the record describes exactly the facts the drive ran against. Declaring a sensor says where a divergence came from and claims nothing about exactness, so declaring them alone leaves every transition [constant NetwPredict.DOMAIN_OUT].
True while the authoritative body is asleep. Corrections pause while it is, so a sleeping body is never nudged awake by one. A game writes it when its own body sleeps and wakes.
What this entity's engine counted, on a [NetwPredictStats].

How far the pose may be wrong, in the pose field's own units, before a recovery restores everything instead of withholding the fields declared [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only]. An error that large means something really went wrong, such as a wall bounce or a teleport, rather than a field slowly drifting, and past it the predicted body holds nothing worth keeping. The error is measured over the fields that declared a [method NetwPropertyConfig.carry_along] or named their own [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_at]. An entity with neither has no pose to measure, and every recovery it makes restores everything. This is the default for such a field that named no distance of its own, and it only means anything for fields in the same units. A pose spanning metres, radians and radians per second cannot be served by one number, so a field in any other unit declares [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_at] rather than inheriting one that means nothing for it. Each field is compared against its own distance, and any one of them reaching it is enough.

Returns whether the path to a proposed pose is clear. A correction that moves a body to where it should be now, across a path nobody checked, is how a body arrives inside a wall, so that correction is only available once this is declared. An unset or invalid [Callable] leaves it unavailable. It is called as [code]corridor(current, proposed)[/code], and only after everything the engine can decide for itself has already passed, so it is the game's last word rather than its first. A game rejecting a move the engine would have rejected anyway is paying for a call that changes nothing.

Samples what this peer's body actually touched on the transition just solved. It is called once per solved transition and returns the colliders the body touched, which is what lets a divergence be blamed on a contact. An unset or invalid [Callable] leaves that unknown, which is the absence of an observation rather than an observation that nothing was touched.

signal.name: divergence_detected
episode_closed
signal.description: Emitted when a run of agreement long enough to be trusted closes an episode. [param report] is shaped as [signal episode_opened] describes. It is a copy, and it stays valid after later rows have pushed out the row it names.

signal.name: episode_fallback
signal.description: Emitted when an episode runs out of evidence to recover with and the entity starts following authority instead. [param report] is shaped as [signal episode_opened] describes. The entity keeps sending its input while it has stopped predicting ahead.

signal.name: episode_opened
signal.description: Emitted when a settled comparison diverges far enough to act on and opens an episode. [param report] is a copy of the episode record. The attribution is a [enum NetwPredict.Attribution], each operator a [enum NetwPredict.Operator] with a [enum NetwPredict.OperatorOutcome], and the disposition state a [enum NetwPredict.EpisodeState]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴id int ┠╴generator Dictionary ┃ ┠╴transition int ┃ ┠╴boundary NetwPredict.Attribution ┃ ┖╴row Dictionary ┠╴operators Array[Dictionary] ┃ ┠╴operator NetwPredict.Operator ┃ ┠╴basis int ┃ ┠╴eligible bool ┃ ┠╴applied bool ┃ ┠╴eligibility Dictionary ┃ ┠╴outcome NetwPredict.OperatorOutcome ┃ ┖╴write Dictionary ┠╴contraction Array[Dictionary] ┃ ┖╴ transition, meter, agrees, write_id ┠╴disposition Dictionary ┃ ┠╴state NetwPredict.EpisodeState ┃ ┠╴non_contraction_used int ┃ ┠╴closure_used int ┃ ┠╴closed_transition int ┃ ┠╴fallback_transition int ┃ ┠╴demoted bool ┃ ┠╴breach_transition int ┃ ┠╴breach_witness Dictionary ┃ ┠╴resume_ack_age int ┃ ┠╴quarantine_target int ┃ ┠╴quarantine_clean_run int ┃ ┠╴reseed_transition int ┃ ┠╴aligned_transition int ┃ ┖╴evidence_dropped int ┖╴reopen_chain Array[int] [/codeblock] [code]generator.row[/code] is the recorded row for that transition, and its [code]witness_detail[/code] carries the contact behind the witness fingerprint. A run that began before the kept window starts reads [constant GENERATOR_UNKNOWN_BEYOND_RETENTION]. Later diverging rows appear under [code]taint[/code], and failures that began on their own appear under [code]secondary_generators[/code]. An operator that was rejected has [code]outcome = -1[/code] and an empty [code]write[/code]. Each series is kept only to a bounded window, because an episode has no limit on how long it may stay open. A trim keeps the newest entries and counts what it dropped, so a truncated series can be told apart from a short one.

signal.name: recovered
signal.description: Emitted after a recovery wrote the body. It names the transition it went back to, how far each field moved as [code]after - before[/code], whether the move was large enough to be a teleport, and what the divergence was blamed on. An angle's change is given as the shorter way around. A recovery is one write, so this fires once per recovery and [param deltas] is the whole of it. A game does not have to absorb them by hand. Under [constant NetwMultiplayer.LIVE_MODE_CHASE] the smoothing already turns each one into an offset that decays away, reset for each recovery and snapped through on a teleport. [codeblock] entity.interpolation.live_mode = NetwMultiplayer.LIVE_MODE_CHASE api.display_set_param(entity.rid, NetwMultiplayer.DISPLAY_PARAM_CHASE_GLIDE_TIME, 0.15) [/codeblock] A recovery that moved nothing does not fire this at all, because a signal carrying no change reads exactly like one that repaired the body. [param deltas] is what the recovery wrote rather than what the node reads back now, because a setter backed by the physics server may not reach its node until the next physics frame, and reading it now would report no movement.

signal.name: state_evaluated
signal.description: Emitted every time state arrives on the owning client, carrying the full divergence including values under [member divergence_epsilon], and what the comparison decided. [param diverged] is what was decided and not what was written. A comparison that found a divergence reports it here whether or not anything was written for it, and several paths deliberately write nothing, such as the evidence running out or an operator waiting on a witness. Those still report true, so a reader that only watches sees a divergence the engine chose not to act on. [signal recovered] is the signal for the write. A frame that reached no comparison at all still fires this, with a zero divergence and no correction, so a listener sees the frame arrive rather than losing it silently. [signal divergence_detected] fires only when a transition actually disagrees. A drift that grows tick over tick and never crosses [member divergence_epsilon] is heard here and never there, so anything watching for a drift nothing acted on reads this one. [param divergence] is the worst field alone.

constants.constant: Generator status when the causal fork predates retained rows.
